articles.title: Sensex sinks over 2,000 points in 5 days. How scary do the charts look for next week?
articles.content: Indian markets enter a crucial week with Nifty testing the key 23,600 support after five straight sessions of losses. Rising crude oil prices, weak earnings and global headwinds have turned sentiment bearish, while analysts see 24,000–24,200 as major resistance levels.

articles.title: Crude oil prices rise 10% this week but China enters fray to push for end to Iran war. What’s next?
articles.content: Crude oil futures experienced a significant decline on Friday. This drop followed reports of China's initiative to restart stalled US-Iran peace negotiations. Despite the fall, both Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude are set for weekly gains. Geopolitical developments continue to heavily influence global oil prices and supply concerns. Experts warn of potential price surges if shipping disruptions persist in key waterways.

articles.title: European shares gain as SAP lifts tech stocks; Middle East on watch
articles.content: European shares saw a rise on Friday, recovering from previous losses. Investors reacted positively to select corporate earnings reports and oil price concerns. Germany's DAX index climbed as SAP's cloud backlog growth exceeded expectations. Higher oil prices did not boost energy stocks due to a drop in Neste's performance. Policymakers indicated potential interest rate hikes amid inflation risks.

articles.title: Stocks waver on Wall Street while crude oil prices fall for the first time in a week
articles.content: Stocks saw a mixed close on Wall Street as oil prices declined after a week of gains. Major indexes experienced losses for the week due to escalating U.S. conflict with Iran. Investors also faced new tariffs and persistent inflation concerns impacting the economy. Bond yields eased, providing some relief to the stock market's pressure. European markets advanced while Asian markets closed lower on Friday.

articles.title: NMC health settlement drags Bank of Baroda Q1 net profit down 72%
articles.content: Bank of Baroda's June-quarter profit fell 72% due to a large settlement payment. Other income also declined, impacting the bank's overall financial performance for the period. Shriram Finance reported a 60% increase in its standalone net profit for the first quarter. Bank of India's net profit jumped 36%, and it seeks foreign currency deposits.

articles.title: Yen records biggest weekly drop in over two months, dollar climbs for the week
articles.content: The dollar is set for its biggest weekly gain, buoyed by rising oil prices. The Japanese yen is poised for its largest weekly decline, languishing at 40-year lows. Verbal efforts to support the yen have seen muted results, with officials reiterating readiness to act. Renewed strikes in the Iran war have fanned inflation fears, increasing rate hike expectations.

articles.title: Gold edges up as Brent eases, Mideast developments in focus ahead of Fed meet
articles.content: Gold prices saw a slight increase on Friday as Brent crude oil retreated from highs. Investors are assessing Middle East conflict developments and their inflation implications. Elevated oil prices and rising yields may cap any further recovery.

articles.title: Rupee hits day’s low against US dollar, recovers on RBI support
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of India's interventions prevented the rupee from falling to a new record low.  State-run banks sold dollars, and foreign investor inflows aided the currency's recovery.  High oil prices and importer demand put pressure on the rupee throughout the day.  Brent crude prices retreated after topping one hundred dollars a barrel.  The rupee closed little changed, recovering from its intraday low.

articles.title: BNP Paribas Cardif to acquire Warburg’s 26% in IndiaFirst Life
articles.content: BNP Paribas Cardif will re-enter India's life insurance market soon.  The French insurer is acquiring Warburg Pincus' stake in IndiaFirst Life.  This transaction values the Bank of Baroda-controlled insurer at approximately ten thousand crore rupees.  Bank of Baroda will retain its controlling interest and management control.  BNP Paribas Cardif will hold twenty-six percent of the insurer's shares.

Treasury gains are expected to be under pressure for banks.

articles.title: More banks may join overseas bond run after ICICI Bank’s bumper dollar bond sale
articles.content: ICICI Bank successfully raised one billion dollars through its inaugural dollar bond sale. This strong investor demand allowed the bank to double its initial offering size. The successful transaction signals confidence in Indian bank credit from global investors. Other lenders are now preparing to raise dollar bonds using a subsidized hedging facility. This initiative aims to lower borrowing costs and support capital inflows into India.

articles.title: US stocks today: Nasdaq lags on angst over AI spending ahead of earnings reports
articles.content: U.S. markets closed mixed as the Nasdaq declined on chip stock weakness driven by concerns over heavy AI spending, while the Dow rose and the S&P 500 was nearly flat. Falling oil prices offered support, though geopolitical tensions and tariff developments kept investor sentiment cautious ahead of major tech earnings.

articles.title: American Express Q2 profit rises driven by higher spending and fewer delinquencies
articles.content: American Express has indicated an impressive eight percent growth in profit during the second quarter, largely driven by increased spending from card members and a decline in delinquency rates. The surge in sign-ups for the company's premium offerings showcases their effective customer acquisition strategies. However, it's worth noting that expenses saw a twelve percent rise due to marketing initiatives and product updates, marking a notable investment in future growth.

articles.title: ACC Q1 Results: Profit plunges 60% to Rs 147 crore on lower sales
articles.content: ACC Ltd, part of the Adani Group, reported a staggering 60.8% decline in net profit for the June quarter. This drop in profitability can be attributed to a decline in sales volume, resulting in a 7.75% decrease in revenue compared to the previous year. While higher costs impacted earnings, the company noted that premium products gained market share.

articles.title: REC Q1 Results: Net profit dips over 6% to Rs 4,193 crore
articles.content: REC Ltd reported a year-on-year profit decline of six percent for the June quarter, primarily due to lower interest income affecting its consolidated net profit. Additionally, total income dropped compared to the previous year. The company announced an interim dividend of Rs 4.25 per share and declared a final dividend of Rs 1.55 per share for the past fiscal year.

articles.title: Lodha Developers Q1 Results: Profit jumps 2-fold to Rs 1,373 crore
articles.content: Lodha Developers reported a remarkable 100% increase in net profit for the first quarter, showcasing substantial growth in sales bookings, which rose by four percent to reach Rs 4,630 crore. Their total income has significantly outperformed the same quarter last year, marking the highest quarterly profit in the company's history. With confidence in sustaining a twenty percent CAGR, Lodha Developers is optimistic about long-term profit expansion.
